propositions: The test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer test kills its pytest-xdist worker on macOS py3.13 due to exceeding the 300-second per-test timeout budget.

The test's cost is unbounded: it iterates over 884 renderable units in a single monolithic loop, each rendered twice via pandoc spawns, measuring 91.6s idle and 504.8s under CPU saturation (1.7x past the timeout guard).
The crash manifests as worker termination via os._exit(1) from pytest-timeout's thread method, producing no traceback and no assertion text, only 'node down: Not properly terminated'.
The fix parametrizes the equivalence test into chunks of fixed size (_EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK=40) to bound per-test cost independent of corpus growth and load, reducing worst case from 504.8s to 38.05s.
A new test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit guard verifies all 884 units are compared across chunks and that the total remains >= 100.
All 884 units continue to be compared against the oracle with real pandoc at stride 1, preserving the byte-identity property without timeout raise, retry marker, or elapsed-time assertion.
